correctness.rationale: For each p>=2, Q=2^p-1, c=1/(4Q), orbit positions x0=1/Q and xj=2^(p-j)/Q (j>=1) are all distinct. The symmetric confidence set consists of [-c,c] and up to three positive bands and their negatives: I1 around the range 2/Q to 2^(p-2)/Q for p>=3, I2 around 2^(p-1)/Q, I3 around (Q-1)/Q; for p=2, I2 and I3 coincide and I1 is omitted. Their integer/Q offsets have strict margin c for intended trust and >=3c for excluded trust. At x0 the moving agent trusts stubborn opinion 1 only, giving R(x)=(x+1)/2; at the other orbit positions it trusts stubborn 0 only, giving L(x)=x/2. R followed by p-1 halvings forms a least-period-p cycle. A nonempty open c/2-neighborhood follows the same itinerary, errors halve at every step and return multiplier is 2^(-p); hence attraction is genuine, not a fragile point cycle. With <=2 agents, reciprocal averaging reaches consensus or a one-stubborn distance strictly contracts upon any nontrivial step, so no nonconstant cycle; the three-agent count is minimal. Independently checked exact rational transitions/trust/perturbations for representative p including 2..59,120,200. Those finite instances do not prove the universal p theorem; the symbolic integer separation does. Endpoints of confidence bands depend on p.
